title: Hypothesis-driven postmortem and sensorization for stealth capacity saturation
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: During a mid-sized capacity event on 2026-02-27 the Console experienced persistent tail-latency spikes for a subset of tenants even though overall ingress and GPU utilization metrics looked normal. This incident exposed several 'stealth' observability gaps: missing per-tenant KV cache eviction metrics, a dashboard that aggregated away long-tail latencies, and a sampling policy that dropped traces for low-frequency but high-cost code paths. This ticket drives the postmortem follow-ups using a hypothesis-driven approach: instrument missing signals, stabilize dashboards/alerts, and add continuous validation to prevent regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant kv_cache_eviction_rate metric emitted at 1m resolution for all tenants
New console dashboard with pct50/pct95/pct99 tail latency and kv eviction overlays published and shared with SRE/Console PM
Sampling policy updated and deployed to retain traces for requests with kv_eviction=true or response_time>1s
Alerting rule for sudden increase in per-tenant kv_cache_eviction_rate and tail-latency anomalies created
E2E synthetic test added to CI that simulates skewed tenant load and validates metric emission and dashboard queries
investigation_summary: Timeline: 2026-02-27 03:10 UTC - first SLO breach in p99 latency for console routes; initial paging notified SREs
Initial hypothesis 1: bursty upstream ingress - rejected because aggregate ingress and queue depth metrics remained stable
Initial hypothesis 2: model-side regression - rejected after canary showed no change in tokens/sec or model latency
Confirmed: a small percentage of tenants experienced repeated KV cache misses leading to prolonged KV fetch paths and high CPU soft-lock contention on a subset of serving nodes

Root cause(s): 1) No per-tenant eviction metric - existing metrics aggregated across tenants; 2) Dashboard rollups used a sampled p99 that dropped low-frequency tails; 3) Trace sampling logic excluded traces without known route tags, dropping the exact requests that surfaced the regression; 4) Metric ingestion cardinality filter excluded tenant label patterns introduced by a recent org rename script
decisions: Add per-tenant kv_cache_eviction_rate metric emitted from runtime and ingested without cardinality filtering
Create a dedicated Console 'tail-latency' dashboard that uses raw tenant-scoped series rather than pre-aggregated rollups
Update tracing sampler to include a deterministic include-list for span attribute kv.eviction=true and response_time>800ms
Backfill short-term telemetry by running a targeted log + trace capture for past 48h where raw logs exist
Enforce a metric-schema gate in CI to catch future accidental label-whitelisting changes

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: per-tenant metrics can increase cardinality and cost - Mitigation: use stable hash-bucketing and sampling on low-volume tenants; monitor ingestion cost after rollout
Risk: increased trace retention for tails may raise storage - Mitigation: apply retention-to-hotspot mapping and only keep enriched traces for 7 days
Risk: dashboards might produce noisy alerts initially - Mitigation: use dynamic baselining and escalations only after 2 consecutive windows
Risk: rollback required if ingest costs spike - Mitigation: feature-flag metric emission and staged rollout to 10% of tenants
